details:
Using GetComponent<ScaleConstraint>() is much slower than using GetComponent<Rigidbody>() for no particular reason. And using GetComponent(typeof(ScaleConstraint)) has better performance than the generic counterpart to the point that it's on par with the generic GetComponent<Rigidbody>().
The following tests were run using this script compiled with UdonSharp https://gist.github.com/Merlin-san/7b785bda752798115522010f8f3983c6
The baseline time to do 10,000 iterations on a loop in editor with the attached script is around 13.4ms on my computer. Enabling the generic GetComponent<Rigidbody>() call brings the loop time up to around 17.5ms which means the GetComponent<Rigidbody>() takes about 4.1ms to run 10,000 times in editor.
Enabling only the GetComponent<ScaleConstraint>() brings the time to execute up to 19.5ms which means GetComponent<ScaleConstraint>() takes about 6.1ms or 50% longer than GetComponent<Rigidbody>() for no reason.
Both GetComponent(typeof(Rigidbody)) and GetComponent(typeof(ScaleConstraint)) take about 4.4ms so there’s something wrong with the generic version of GetComponent<ScaleConstraint>(). In U# the generic version of this gets converted to an extern call to “UnityEngineAnimationsScaleConstraint.__GetComponent__T”.
Running the code as actual C# instead of U# on Udon, has the loop taking 0.04ms without any GetComponent calls. Using either GetComponent<Rigidbody>() or GetComponent<ScaleConstraint>() makes it take about 0.6ms on average. So there isn’t a disparity in performance on C#.
If the necessity for pushing the System.Type to the input arguments for the __GetComponent__T variants is removed when you look at this, it would be a welcome change since right now U# needs to redundantly push the System.Type of the component type you’re attempting to get despite every type having a specific function defined for it. Like in this case “UnityEngineAnimationsScaleConstraint.__GetComponent__T” should return a ScaleConstraint type and that’s already defined by the name of the method so we shouldn’t need to redundantly push the type. 
This canny may also be relevant: https://vrchat.canny.io/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-bugs/p/getcomponentst-functions-are-not-defined-internally-for-vrcsdk3-components

edit:
Intentionally breaking the U# compiler to always call the extern "UnityEngineCollider.__GetComponent__T" no matter the type and pass in the correct System.Type for the requested type still works for any type. I'm able to get a ScaleConstraint type by pushing a System.Type of the ScaleConstraint type and calling the "UnityEngineCollider.__GetComponent__T" extern. Which indicates that the specialized GetComponent_T functions are probably doing a redundant lookup with a giant switch statement or something when they already should know what type they need to return since the return type is specified by the method extern signature in this case.
title: Performance disparity between GetComponent<T> on two different types
